full_judgment:
2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that respondent Nos. 1-8 as plaintiffs instituted Partition Suit No. 144 of 1984 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Jamalpur, stating, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Amanu Mollah and C.S. record was prepared in his name. Amanu Mollah died leaving his wife Moijan Bewa, only son Zamanu Mollah and only daughter Poiron Bibi. Though C.S. Khatian was not prepared in the name of Poiron Bibi, she was the successor-in-interest of Amanu Mollah. Poiron Bibi died leaving behind husband Kalu Mondal, mother Moijan Bewa, bother Zamanu Molla (defendant No. 1) and only daughter Khateman @ Khatun Bewa (defendant No. 4); that Moijan transferred her share in the suit land, i.e. 42 decimals of land to the plaintiffs 27 years previously and gave possession to them by way of a kabala dated 10.06.1958. Defendant No. 4 Khateman @ Khatun Bewa sold 52 decimals of land to the plaintiffs by a registered kabala dated 05.02.1972 and handed over possession to them and in this way the plaintiffs got 94 decimals of land. Defendant Nos. 5-9 are the sons of defendant No. 1 and they are step brothers of the plaintiffs. Defendant Nos. 5-9 are trying to grab the suit land; the plaintiffs asked defendant Nos. 5-9 to partition of the suit land amicably in the month of Boishakh, 1391 B.S. but the defendants refused, hence the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 5-9 contested the suit by filing a written objection denying the material allegations of the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Amanu Molla who died leaving defendant No. 1 as only son and widow Moijan Bewa as heirs; that Moijan Bewa died leaving only son defendant No. 1 as her heir and in this way defendant No. 1 got 16 annas share in the suit land and he continued to own and possess the suit land adversely against the plaintiffs and others. The plaintiffs are the sons of defendant No. 1 from his first wife. The plaintiffs are elder brothers of defendant Nos. 5-9 and as such the plaintiffs were entrusted to look after the properties and taking this opportunity the plaintiffs, in collusion with others, managed to include their names with defendant No. 1 in the relevant R.O.R. Khatian. Defendant No. 1 came to know about these fraudulent activities of the plaintiffs when the R.O.R. record was finally published. Defendant No. 1 drove away the plaintiffs from their homestead and from the suit land. Thereafter, the plaintiffs went away from the suit land relinquished their claims on it and erected homestead in Shital Kursha village; that the plaintiffs created some false, forged and ante-dated deeds showing Poiron Bibi as a heir of Amanu Molla who was not in existence. While he was in possession of the suit land, defendant No. 1 transferred 2.59 acres of land to defendant Nos. 5-9 by way of a registered Hebanama dated 13.11.1968 and gave possession to them. Defendant No. 1 transferred 40 decimals of land to defendant Nos. 5-9 by a registered Heba-bil-Ewaj deed dated 19.06.1983 and delivered possession to them. The plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the suit land and they instituted, the suit with oblique motives and hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
